555.explanation: In formal discussion, a question with need before the subject is often rhetorical: the writer doesn't expect an answer. Need I say more? means 'the point is already clear'.
examples: Need I say more?
Need we really spend so much money?
Need I remind you of the rules?

uk.explanation: В офіційній дискусії запитання з need перед підметом часто риторичне: автор не чекає відповіді. Need I say more? означає «і так усе зрозуміло».

557.explanation: Use you ought to + verb to give advice. It means almost the same as you should, but it is a little more formal and less common. Don't forget to: ought to, not ought.
examples: You ought to see a doctor.
You ought to call your mum more often.
You ought to get some sleep.

uk.explanation: You ought to + verb — так даємо пораду. Це майже те саме, що you should, але трохи офіційніше й рідше вживається. Не забувайте про to: ought to, а не ought.

559.explanation: Use ought to + verb to talk about how things should be in an ideal world, often when the real situation is different.
examples: Everyone ought to have a safe home.
Public transport ought to be cheaper.
Children ought to spend more time outside.

uk.explanation: Ought to + verb кажемо про те, як усе мало б бути в ідеальному світі, часто коли насправді ситуація інша.

560.explanation: Use there ought to be + noun to say that something should exist but doesn't. It is common when you complain or suggest a change.
examples: There ought to be more buses at night.
There ought to be a law against this.
There ought to be a café in the park.

uk.explanation: There ought to be + noun кажемо, що щось мало б існувати, але його немає. Так часто говорять, коли скаржаться або пропонують зміни.

561.explanation: Add really before ought to, or between ought and to in formal writing, to make advice or an opinion stronger: really ought to.
examples: You really ought to see this film.
We really ought to leave now.
They really ought to fix this road.

uk.explanation: Додайте really перед ought to — або, в офіційному письмі, між ought і to, — щоб порада чи думка звучала сильніше: really ought to.

562.explanation: Use ought to have + past participle to say that something was the right thing to do in the past, but it didn't happen. It is close to should have.
examples: You ought to have told me earlier.
We ought to have booked a table.
They ought to have asked for help.

uk.explanation: Ought to have + past participle кажемо, що в минулому варто було щось зробити, але цього не сталося. Це близько до should have.

563.explanation: Use ought to + verb to say that something is likely or expected, because that is the normal result. It means the same as should: The parcel ought to arrive tomorrow.
examples: The parcel ought to arrive tomorrow.
It's a short walk — it ought to take ten minutes.
With all that practice, she ought to win.

uk.explanation: Ought to + verb кажемо, що щось імовірне або очікуване, бо це звичайний результат. Це те саме, що should: The parcel ought to arrive tomorrow.

569.explanation: Use Shall I + verb? to offer to do something for someone. It means 'Do you want me to…?'
examples: Shall I open the window?
Shall I carry your bag?
Shall I call you a taxi?

uk.explanation: Shall I + verb? — так пропонуємо щось зробити для когось. Це означає «Хочете, я…?»

570.explanation: Use Shall we + verb? to suggest doing something together. It means 'Do you want to…?' or 'Let's…'.
examples: Shall we go to the cinema?
Shall we meet at six?
What shall we do tonight?

uk.explanation: Shall we + verb? — так пропонуємо зробити щось разом. Це означає «Може, …?» або «Давайте…».

571.explanation: In statements, I shall or we shall + verb talks about plans, intentions and promises. It means the same as I will, but sounds formal and is common in letters and emails.
examples: I shall be free on Sunday evening.
We shall send you the tickets next week.
I shall do my best.

uk.explanation: У ствердних реченнях I shall або we shall + verb кажемо про плани, наміри й обіцянки. Це те саме, що I will, але звучить офіційно й часто трапляється в листах.

572.explanation: Use What shall I…? or Shall I…? to ask someone for advice about what to do.
examples: What shall I wear to the party?
Where shall I put these boxes?
Shall I tell her the truth?

uk.explanation: What shall I…? або Shall I…? — так просимо поради, що робити.

574.explanation: In laws, contracts and official rules, shall with any subject gives an order or an obligation: it means must. Shall not means must not. You won't hear this in conversation.
examples: The tenant shall pay the rent monthly.
Visitors shall not enter this area.
All members shall follow these rules.

uk.explanation: У законах, договорах і офіційних правилах shall з будь-яким підметом виражає наказ чи обов'язок: означає must. Shall not означає must not. У розмові так не кажуть.

575.explanation: In formal writing, shall can replace will in the main clause after an if-clause, usually with I or we. It often sounds serious, like a warning: If…, we shall….
examples: If we get no reply, we shall contact our lawyer.
If it rains, we shall stay inside.
If you are late, I shall start without you.

uk.explanation: В офіційному письмі shall може замінити will у головній частині після if-речення, зазвичай з I або we. Часто це звучить серйозно, як попередження: If…, we shall….

576.explanation: Shall + verb can say what you think will happen in the future, as a formal alternative to will. It is most natural with I and we; We shall see means 'we'll find out later'.
examples: We shall see what happens.
I shall never forget that day.
We shall know the results soon.

uk.explanation: Shall + verb може передбачати майбутнє як офіційна альтернатива will. Найприродніше звучить з I та we; We shall see означає «побачимо згодом».

580.explanation: Use should + verb to give advice or say what is a good idea. Shouldn't means it is not a good idea. The verb after should has no to.
examples: You should drink more water.
You shouldn't go to bed so late.
Should I buy this jacket?

uk.explanation: Should + verb — так даємо пораду або кажемо, що щось добра ідея. Shouldn't означає, що це погана ідея. Дієслово після should — без to.

581.explanation: Use should + verb, often with we, to suggest a plan or an idea: We should go to the beach. It sounds a bit stronger than We could….
examples: We should go to the beach on Sunday.
Maybe we should take a taxi.
We should meet for coffee sometime.

uk.explanation: Should + verb, часто з we, — так пропонуємо план чи ідею: We should go to the beach. Це звучить трохи наполегливіше, ніж We could….

582.explanation: Add the question tag shouldn't we? or shouldn't I? to the end of a suggestion to ask if the other person agrees.
examples: We should leave soon, shouldn't we?
I should call her, shouldn't I?
We should buy a present, shouldn't we?

uk.explanation: Додайте розділове запитання shouldn't we? або shouldn't I? у кінці пропозиції, щоб спитати, чи співрозмовник погоджується.

585.explanation: Use should + verb to say how things ought to be in an ideal world, often when the real situation is different.
examples: Everyone should have the right to study.
Cities should have more parks.
Medicine should be free for children.

uk.explanation: Should + verb кажемо, як усе мало б бути в ідеальному світі, часто коли насправді ситуація інша.

586.explanation: Use should + verb to say that something will probably happen, because that is what you expect. It should be fun means 'I expect it will be fun'.
examples: It should be a great party.
The train should arrive at five.
This shouldn't take long.

uk.explanation: Should + verb кажемо, що щось, імовірно, станеться, бо ви цього очікуєте. It should be fun означає «гадаю, буде весело».

587.explanation: In a story, You should have seen or heard…! is not a real regret. It means 'it was amazing — I wish you had been there', and makes the story more exciting.
examples: You should have seen his face!
You should have heard the noise!
You should have been there — it was brilliant.

uk.explanation: В розповіді You should have seen чи heard…! — не справжній жаль. Це означає «було неймовірно — шкода, що тебе там не було» і робить історію цікавішою.

588.explanation: Use should have + past participle to say that something was the right thing to do in the past, but it didn't happen. Shouldn't have + past participle says something was a mistake.
examples: I should have studied harder.
You shouldn't have said that.
We should have left earlier.

uk.explanation: Should have + past participle кажемо, що в минулому варто було щось зробити, але цього не сталося. Shouldn't have + past participle означає, що щось було помилкою.

589.explanation: When someone gives you a present, say You shouldn't have! to thank them politely. It isn't criticism: it means 'thank you, that was very kind'.
examples: Flowers? Oh, you shouldn't have!
Thank you for the present — you shouldn't have!
You shouldn't have spent so much on me.

uk.explanation: Коли вам дарують подарунок, You shouldn't have! — ввічлива подяка. Це не докір, а «дякую, це дуже мило».

592.explanation: Use should be + -ing to say what you expect to be happening at a certain time.
examples: They should be arriving about now.
This time tomorrow we should be flying to Rome.
The kids should be sleeping by nine.

uk.explanation: Should be + -ing кажемо, що, як ми очікуємо, відбуватиметься в певний момент.

593.explanation: Use should be or shouldn't be + -ing to say what is right or wrong to be doing, often when the real situation is different.
examples: You should be studying, not watching TV.
He shouldn't be driving when he's so tired.
We should be doing more to help.

uk.explanation: Should be або shouldn't be + -ing кажемо, що правильно чи неправильно зараз робити, часто коли насправді відбувається інше.

594.explanation: In formal English, put should after if to make a future situation sound less likely: 'if by any chance…'. It is common in instructions, letters and emails.
examples: If you should need anything, just call me.
If something should happen, call 112.
If you should change your mind, let me know.

uk.explanation: В офіційній англійській should після if робить майбутню ситуацію менш імовірною: «якщо раптом…». Так часто пишуть в інструкціях і листах.

595.explanation: Even more formally, drop if and put should before the subject: Should you need help, …. It is typical at the end of business letters and emails.
examples: Should you have any questions, please contact me.
Should the flight be late, we will wait.
Should you need more information, call our office.

uk.explanation: Ще офіційніше — прибрати if і поставити should перед підметом: Should you need help, …. Так типово закінчують ділові листи.

598.explanation: Use used to + base verb for things that happened again and again, or were true, in the past but are not true now. The negative is didn't use to.
examples: I used to play football every weekend.
She used to live in Odesa.
We didn't use to have a car.

uk.explanation: Used to + base verb кажемо про те, що регулярно відбувалося або було правдою в минулому, але тепер уже ні. Заперечення — didn't use to.

601.explanation: In a story, add as + pronoun + used to + verb to give background: how someone used to describe or name something. It often highlights something unusual: 'as she used to call him'.
examples: He married Nellie, 'my angel' as he used to call her.
She worked for peanuts, as she used to say.
It was a dream, as my father used to say.

uk.explanation: В розповіді as + займенник + used to + verb додає тло: як хтось колись описував чи називав щось. Часто це підкреслює щось незвичне: «як вона його називала».

604.explanation: Use will + verb, often I'll, for a plan or decision you make at the moment of speaking. The verb after will has no to.
examples: I'll call you tomorrow.
It's cold — I'll close the window.
I'll have the soup, please.

uk.explanation: Will + verb, часто I'll, кажемо про план чи рішення, яке ухвалюємо просто під час розмови. Дієслово після will — без to.

605.explanation: Use if + present simple, then will + verb, to talk about a possible future situation and its result: If it rains, we'll stay home. Don't use will in the if-part.
examples: If it rains, we'll stay at home.
If you study, you'll pass the exam.
I'll help you if I have time.

uk.explanation: If + present simple, а потім will + verb — так говоримо про можливу ситуацію в майбутньому та її наслідок: If it rains, we'll stay home. У частині з if will не вживаємо.

608.explanation: Use Will you + verb? or a wh- word + will to ask about someone's plans or decisions for the future.
examples: Will you come to my party?
What will you do after school?
When will you be back?

uk.explanation: Will you + verb? або питальне слово + will — так питаємо про чиїсь плани чи рішення на майбутнє.

609.explanation: Use I'll + verb to offer help or say you are happy to do something. Won't can mean someone refuses: He won't listen.
examples: I'll carry that for you.
Don't worry, I'll pay.
The door won't open.

uk.explanation: I'll + verb — так пропонуємо допомогу або кажемо, що охоче щось зробимо. Won't може означати відмову: He won't listen.

610.explanation: Use Will you + verb? to ask someone to do something. It is direct, so it is best with family and friends.
examples: Will you help me with this box?
Will you close the door?
Will you call me later?

uk.explanation: Will you + verb? — так просимо когось щось зробити. Це досить прямо, тож найкраще підходить для рідних і друзів.

611.explanation: Use will + verb for fixed plans and timetabled events in the future, often with a date or time.
examples: The meeting will start at 10 am.
The course will finish on 20th June.
The shop will be closed on Monday.

uk.explanation: Will + verb кажемо про тверді плани й події за розкладом у майбутньому, часто з датою чи часом.

612.explanation: Use will + verb to say what you think will happen in the future. It often comes after I think or I'm sure.
examples: I think it will rain tomorrow.
You'll love this book.
Prices will go up next year.

uk.explanation: Will + verb кажемо, що, на нашу думку, станеться в майбутньому. Часто стоїть після I think або I'm sure.

613.explanation: Use Will you please + verb? or will you + verb at the end to make firm requests and commands. It can sound impatient.
examples: Will you please be quiet?
Will you please send me the form?
Sit down, will you?

uk.explanation: Will you please + verb? або will you наприкінці — так висловлюємо наполегливі прохання й накази. Це може звучати нетерпляче.

614.explanation: Use will + verb to describe what someone usually does, or what something typically does, in general. Adverbs like often, usually and sometimes are common here.
examples: My cat will sleep anywhere.
She'll often read until midnight.
Boys will be boys.

uk.explanation: Will + verb описує, що хтось зазвичай робить або що щось типово робить, загалом. Тут часто вживаються often, usually та sometimes.

615.explanation: Use will + verb, stressed and not shortened, to describe someone's typical behaviour that you find annoying.
examples: He will leave his socks on the floor!
She will talk during films.
They will keep calling me at night.

uk.explanation: Will + verb, з наголосом і без скорочення, описує типову поведінку, яка вас дратує.

617.explanation: Use I would like to invite you to… to make a polite invitation, for example in a letter or email. The short form is I'd like to.
examples: I'd like to invite you to my birthday party.
We would like to invite you to dinner.
I'd like to invite you to our wedding.

uk.explanation: I would like to invite you to… — так ввічливо запрошуємо, наприклад у листі. Коротка форма — I'd like to.

618.explanation: Use would like + noun or would like to + verb to say what you want politely. It is softer than want. The short form is I'd like.
examples: I'd like a cup of tea, please.
I would like to visit London.
Would you like some cake?

uk.explanation: Would like + noun або would like to + verb — так ввічливо кажемо, чого хочемо. Це м'якше, ніж want. Коротка форма — I'd like.

622.explanation: Use would + verb to talk about an imagined situation: something that is not real, or not happening now.
examples: A holiday by the sea would be perfect.
I would never do that.
It would be nice to live near the park.

uk.explanation: Would + verb кажемо про уявну ситуацію: щось нереальне або таке, що зараз не відбувається.

623.explanation: Use it would be + adjective + to + verb to make a suggestion politely: It would be nice to…, It would be better to….
examples: It would be nice to meet on Saturday.
It would be better to take the train.
It would be great to see you again.

uk.explanation: It would be + adjective + to + verb — так ввічливо щось пропонуємо: It would be nice to…, It would be better to….

624.explanation: Use would + verbs like prefer, love or rather to talk about wishes and preferences politely: I'd prefer…, I'd love to…, I'd rather….
examples: I'd prefer to stay at home tonight.
I'd love to come to your party.
I'd rather have tea than coffee.

uk.explanation: Would + дієслова на кшталт prefer, love чи rather — так ввічливо говоримо про бажання й уподобання: I'd prefer…, I'd love to…, I'd rather….

625.explanation: Use if + past simple, then would + verb, to talk about an imagined situation. It is common for advice: If I were you, I'd….
examples: If I were you, I'd take the job.
If I had more time, I would learn Spanish.
What would you do if you won?

uk.explanation: If + past simple, а потім would + verb — так говоримо про уявну ситуацію. Це поширено в порадах: If I were you, I'd….

630.explanation: Use would + verb to talk about the future from a point in the past: something that was still in the future then.
examples: I knew she would be late.
He promised he would call.
We thought it would rain.

uk.explanation: Would + verb кажемо про майбутнє з погляду минулого: про те, що тоді ще мало статися.

631.explanation: Use would have + past participle to talk about an imagined past: what was possible, but didn't happen, often after an if-clause.
examples: I would have come, but I was ill.
If I'd known, I would have helped.
She would have loved this place.

uk.explanation: Would have + past participle кажемо про уявне минуле: про те, що було можливим, але не сталося, часто після if-речення.

632.explanation: Use would with verbs like say, advise, recommend or imagine to make an opinion less direct and more polite: I would say…, I would recommend….
examples: I would say it's the best option.
I'd recommend the fish.
I would imagine they're tired.

uk.explanation: Would з дієсловами на кшталт say, advise, recommend чи imagine робить думку менш прямою і ввічливішою: I would say…, I would recommend….

633.explanation: Use Would you + verb? to make a polite request. Would you mind + -ing? is even more polite.
examples: Would you open the window, please?
Would you mind waiting a moment?
Would you mind helping me?

uk.explanation: Would you + verb? — так ввічливо просимо. Would you mind + -ing? звучить ще ввічливіше.

634.explanation: When you report what someone said, will usually becomes would after said, told or promised. 'I'll come' becomes She said she would come.
examples: She said she would come on Friday.
He told me I would like it.
They promised they would help.

uk.explanation: Коли переказуємо чужі слова, will після said, told чи promised зазвичай стає would. 'I'll come' перетворюється на She said she would come.

635.explanation: Use wouldn't + verb to say that someone refused to do something in the past, or that something didn't work.
examples: The driver wouldn't wait for us.
My parents wouldn't let me go.
The car wouldn't start this morning.

uk.explanation: Wouldn't + verb кажемо, що хтось у минулому відмовлявся щось робити або що щось не працювало.

636.explanation: Use would + verb to talk about things that happened again and again in the past, often in stories and memories. It works only for actions, not states.
examples: My grandfather would sit in the garden for hours.
Every summer we would go to the sea.
She would always bring us sweets.

uk.explanation: Would + verb кажемо про те, що повторювалося в минулому, часто в розповідях і спогадах. Це працює лише для дій, не для станів.

639.explanation: Use probably to show you are not sure, and definitely to show you are sure. Put the adverb after be, or before the main verb: It's probably in the car. She definitely knows.
examples: It's probably in the kitchen.
He definitely wants to come.
It's definitely going to rain.

uk.explanation: Probably показує, що ви не впевнені, а definitely — що впевнені. Прислівник ставимо після be або перед основним дієсловом: It's probably in the car. She definitely knows.

641.explanation: Use adverbs like certainly, definitely and obviously to make a statement stronger. They show that you are completely sure or really mean it. Put them after be or an auxiliary, or before the main verb.
examples: I will certainly call you on Friday.
I definitely recommend this hotel.
You obviously can't work all day.

uk.explanation: Прислівники на кшталт certainly, definitely й obviously роблять твердження сильнішим. Вони показують, що ви цілком упевнені або справді маєте це на увазі. Ставимо їх після be чи допоміжного дієслова або перед основним дієсловом.

642.explanation: Put an adverb like probably, certainly or surely after a modal verb to change how strong it sounds. Probably makes advice or a prediction softer; certainly makes it stronger: modal verb + adverb + base verb.
examples: You should probably take an umbrella.
You would certainly enjoy the trip.
We can surely find a cheaper hotel.

uk.explanation: Прислівник на кшталт probably, certainly чи surely після модального дієслова змінює, наскільки сильно воно звучить. Probably пом'якшує пораду чи прогноз, certainly — підсилює: modal verb + adverb + base verb.

643.explanation: Add possibly after could + subject to make a request extra polite. It shows you know you are asking for something that may not be easy: Could you possibly…? or Could I possibly…?
examples: Could you possibly help me with this form?
Could I possibly leave a bit early today?
Could we possibly meet on Thursday instead?

uk.explanation: Додайте possibly після could + підмет, щоб прохання звучало особливо ввічливо. Так ви показуєте, що розумієте: просите про щось, що може бути непросто зробити: Could you possibly…? або Could I possibly…?

644.explanation: Use not necessarily to say that something is often true, but not in every case. It lets you disagree gently with a general idea by pointing to exceptions. Necessarily comes straight after not or a short negative: isn't necessarily, doesn't necessarily.
examples: Expensive food isn't necessarily better.
A big city doesn't necessarily mean a better life.
Older people are not necessarily wiser.

uk.explanation: Not necessarily кажемо, коли щось часто правда, але не завжди. Так можна м'яко не погодитися із загальною думкою, вказавши на винятки. Necessarily стоїть одразу після not або короткого заперечення: isn't necessarily, doesn't necessarily.

645.explanation: Not necessarily can be a complete answer on its own. It means 'no, not always' or 'that's not the only possibility', and it sounds softer than a simple no. The word not comes first.
examples: Is the cheapest option the worst? Not necessarily.
So you'll need a car there? Not necessarily.
Does rain mean the match is cancelled? Not necessarily.

uk.explanation: Not necessarily може бути цілою відповіддю. Вона означає «ні, не завжди» або «це не єдиний варіант» і звучить м'якше, ніж просто no. Слово not стоїть першим.

646.explanation: An adverb of certainty can be a full answer by itself: Definitely, Certainly, Absolutely, Probably. It is shorter and more natural than repeating the whole sentence. Add not for a negative answer: Probably not, Definitely not.
examples: Would you go there again? Definitely.
Can I borrow your pen? Certainly.
Will they win tonight? Probably not.

uk.explanation: Прислівник упевненості може бути повною відповіддю: Definitely, Certainly, Absolutely, Probably. Це коротше й природніше, ніж повторювати все речення. Для заперечної відповіді додайте not: Probably not, Definitely not.

659.explanation: For emphasis, use such a + adjective + singular noun, and such + adjective + plural or uncountable noun: such a nice day, such good friends. Such goes before a, not after it.
examples: It was such a nice day.
They are such good friends.
I've never had such delicious food.

uk.explanation: Для підсилення вживаємо such a + adjective + іменник в однині та such + adjective + іменник у множині або незлічуваний: such a nice day, such good friends. Such стоїть перед a, а не після нього.
examples: Був такий гарний день.
Вони такі добрі друзі.
Я ніколи не їв такої смачної їжі.

661.explanation: After a superlative + noun (the best film, the funniest person), add a clause with the present perfect or past perfect to mean of all the ones I have ever…: the best film I've ever seen. Which / that is usually left out, and ever is common.
examples: She's the funniest person I've ever met.
It's the best pizza I've ever had.
It was the worst trip we had ever taken.

uk.explanation: Після найвищого ступеня + іменник (the best film, the funniest person) додаємо речення в present perfect або past perfect зі значенням «з усіх, які я коли-небудь…»: the best film I've ever seen. Which / that зазвичай пропускають, а ever вживається часто.
examples: Вона найвеселіша людина, яку я будь-коли зустрічав.
Це найкраща піца, яку я коли-небудь їла.
Це була найгірша подорож, яку ми будь-коли мали.

662.explanation: For shops, surgeries and people's homes, you can leave out the noun after 's, because everyone knows which place you mean: the dentist's, my grandma's.
examples: I have to go to the dentist's.
We had dinner at my aunt's.
Can you get some bread from the baker's?

uk.explanation: Коли йдеться про крамниці, кабінети лікарів і чиїсь домівки, іменник після 's можна пропустити, бо всі розуміють, про яке місце мова: the dentist's, my grandma's.
examples: Мені треба сходити до стоматолога.
Ми вечеряли в тітки.
Можеш купити хліба в пекарні?

668.explanation: Start with The thing + clause, then be, then the thing you want to highlight: The thing I enjoyed most was the music. It points the listener to one thing and gives it focus.
examples: The thing I liked most was the swimming pool.
The thing I need now is a holiday.
The thing she hates is waiting.

uk.explanation: Почніть із The thing + clause, далі be, а потім те, що хочете виділити: The thing I enjoyed most was the music. Так увага слухача спрямовується на одну річ.
examples: Найбільше мені сподобався басейн.
Зараз мені потрібна відпустка.
Чого вона терпіти не може, так це чекати.

674.explanation: In academic and business writing, a verb or adjective often becomes a noun (nominalisation): grow → growth, decide → a decision. The action becomes a noun phrase, which sounds more formal and objective.
examples: There has been a sharp increase in prices.
The decision to close the factory surprised everyone.
Sales showed steady growth throughout the year.

uk.explanation: В академічному й діловому письмі дієслово чи прикметник часто перетворюють на іменник (номіналізація): grow → growth, decide → a decision. Дія стає іменниковою фразою, що звучить офіційніше й об'єктивніше.
examples: Ціни різко зросли.
Рішення закрити фабрику всіх здивувало.
Упродовж року продажі стабільно зростали.

675.explanation: A what-clause can be a whole noun phrase at the start of a sentence, followed by is / was and the focus: What companies care about is money. It is more formal than The thing (that)…
examples: What companies care about is money.
What I miss most is my mum's cooking.
What surprised me was the price.

uk.explanation: What-речення може бути цілою іменниковою фразою на початку речення, далі is / was і те, на чому наголос: What companies care about is money. Це офіційніше, ніж The thing (that)…
examples: Компаніям важливі лише гроші.
Найбільше мені бракує маминих страв.
Мене здивувала ціна.

703.explanation: Use the passive (be + past participle) with by to add who did something to a thing you are already talking about: I love my phone. It is made by Sony.
examples: It was written by Leo Tolstoy.
This car was bought by my uncle.
The picture was painted by a child.

uk.explanation: Пасив (be + past participle) із by додає, хто виконав дію, до того, про що вже йдеться: I love my phone. It is made by Sony.
examples: Її написав Лев Толстой.
Цю машину купив мій дядько.
Цю картину намалювала дитина.

706.explanation: A passive with by can go inside a relative clause (which, that, who) to add more information about a noun: clothes which are made by famous brands.
examples: I like clothes which are made by famous brands.
We visited a castle that was built by the king.
He met a girl who was loved by everyone.

uk.explanation: Пасив із by може стояти в підрядному означальному реченні (which, that, who), щоб додати інформацію про іменник: clothes which are made by famous brands.
examples: Мені подобається одяг відомих брендів.
Ми відвідали замок, який збудував король.
Він познайомився з дівчиною, яку всі любили.

713.explanation: The end of a sentence is the place for new or important information. So a passive with by puts the focus on who did the action: This piece was composed by Mozart.
examples: This song was written by my brother.
My school was chosen by the TV company.
The film was directed by a young woman.

uk.explanation: Кінець речення — місце для нової чи важливої інформації. Тому пасив із by наголошує на тому, хто виконав дію: This piece was composed by Mozart.
examples: Цю пісню написав мій брат.
Телекомпанія обрала мою школу.
Фільм зняла молода жінка.

714.explanation: The present continuous passive, am / is / are being + past participle, can talk about a future arrangement. A time word shows it is the future: The seminar is being held next week.
examples: The seminar is being held in Kyiv next week.
The new sofa is being delivered on Friday.
We are being visited by the director tomorrow.

uk.explanation: Present continuous passive (am / is / are being + past participle) може означати майбутню домовленість. Слово часу показує, що йдеться про майбутнє: The seminar is being held next week.
examples: Наступного тижня семінар проходитиме в Києві.
Новий диван привезуть у п'ятницю.
Завтра до нас завітає директор.

728.explanation: In essays and reports, use a modal + be + past participle to sum up or give your opinion without saying I or we: Something must be done about it.
examples: Something must be done about the traffic.
A lot could be improved next year.
It can be seen that cycling is cheaper.

uk.explanation: В есе та звітах modal + be + past participle допомагає підсумувати чи висловити думку, не кажучи I чи we: Something must be done about it.
examples: Із заторами треба щось робити.
Наступного року багато що можна покращити.
Видно, що велосипедом дешевше.

729.explanation: Use will be + past participle to talk about something that will be done in the future. It is typical in announcements and formal letters.
examples: The cinema will be renovated next year.
You will be booked into the Palace Hotel.
Your details won't be sent to anyone.

uk.explanation: Will be + past participle вживаємо для того, що буде зроблено в майбутньому. Типово для оголошень і офіційних листів.
examples: Наступного року кінотеатр відремонтують.
Вам забронюють номер у готелі «Палац».
Ваші дані нікому не передаватимуть.

730.explanation: Start a sentence with being + past participle to give background or a reason for the main part: Being born in Mexico, she knows it well. It can also be the subject: Being invited by your boss feels good.
examples: Being born in Mexico, she knows the country well.
Being badly paid, many workers leave.
Being invited by your boss makes you feel noticed.

uk.explanation: Речення можна почати з being + past participle, щоб дати передісторію чи причину для головної частини: Being born in Mexico, she knows it well. Така група може бути й підметом: Being invited by your boss feels good.
examples: Народившись у Мексиці, вона добре знає цю країну.
Оскільки платять погано, багато працівників звільняються.
Коли тебе запрошує начальник, відчуваєш, що тебе помічають.

731.explanation: Use isn't / aren't being + past participle for something that is not happening now, often a situation that is not going well: Students are not being educated equally.
examples: Students are not being educated equally.
The store isn't being promoted enough.
The problem isn't being taken seriously.

uk.explanation: Isn't / aren't being + past participle описує те, чого зараз не відбувається, часто ситуацію, яка йде не так: Students are not being educated equally.
examples: Учні здобувають нерівну освіту.
Магазин недостатньо рекламують.
Проблему не сприймають серйозно.

732.explanation: In formal and academic writing, use it + passive + that to sum up or evaluate without I or we: It can be concluded that… It is an empty subject; the real information is in the that clause.
examples: It can be concluded that the plan works.
It is often argued that zoos protect animals.
It has been found that sales are falling.

uk.explanation: В офіційному та академічному письмі it + passive + that дає змогу підсумувати чи оцінити без I чи we: It can be concluded that… It тут формальний підмет, а головна інформація — у частині з that.
examples: Можна зробити висновок, що план працює.
Часто стверджують, що зоопарки захищають тварин.
З'ясувалося, що продажі падають.

733.explanation: Use having been + past participle to give background that happened before the main part. Not goes before having, and after a preposition use the same form: for having been invited.
examples: Having been taught well, we knew what to do.
Not having been given clear orders, he worked alone.
She came in without having been asked.

uk.explanation: Having been + past participle дає передісторію, що сталася раніше за головну частину. Not стоїть перед having, а після прийменника вживаємо ту саму форму: for having been invited.
examples: Оскільки нас добре навчили, ми знали, що робити.
Не отримавши чітких наказів, він працював сам.
Вона зайшла, хоча її не запрошували.

738.explanation: Use have + object + past participle when someone else does a job for you: I had my car serviced. It can also describe something bad done to you that you didn't arrange: I had my bag stolen.
examples: I had my car serviced last week.
I need to have my hair cut.
She had her phone stolen on the bus.

uk.explanation: Have + object + past participle вживаємо, коли роботу за вас робить хтось інший: I had my car serviced. Так само можна описати щось погане, що з вами сталося з чужої вини: I had my bag stolen.
examples: Минулого тижня я віддав машину на техобслуговування.
Мені треба підстригтися.
У неї вкрали телефон в автобусі.

739.explanation: Use get + person + to-infinitive to say that you persuade someone to do something. It's often not easy: I finally got my son to tidy his room.
examples: I got my brother to help me.
How can we get them to visit more often?
She got her boss to agree.

uk.explanation: Get + person + to-infinitive означає, що ви вмовляєте когось щось зробити. Часто це нелегко: I finally got my son to tidy his room.
examples: Я вмовив брата мені допомогти.
Як нам домогтися, щоб вони приїжджали частіше?
Вона домоглася згоди начальника.

740.explanation: Use get + object + past participle when you arrange for someone else to do something, like have something done but more informal. It often suggests effort: it took hours to get it repaired.
examples: I'm going to get my hair cut tomorrow.
It took hours to get the bus repaired.
She always gets things done.

uk.explanation: Get + object + past participle означає, що ви організовуєте, щоб щось зробив хтось інший, — як have something done, але розмовніше. Часто натякає на зусилля: it took hours to get it repaired.
examples: Завтра я збираюся підстригтися.
Щоб полагодити автобус, знадобилися години.
Вона завжди доводить справи до кінця.

741.explanation: Use get + object + -ing to say that you make someone or something start doing something, and it continues: Your letter got me thinking.
examples: Your question got me thinking.
This band really gets people dancing.
We couldn't get the engine going.

uk.explanation: Get + object + -ing означає, що ви змушуєте когось чи щось почати щось робити, і це триває: Your letter got me thinking.
examples: Твоє запитання змусило мене замислитися.
Під цей гурт усі просто пускаються в танок.
Ми не змогли завести двигун.

742.explanation: Use have + person + base verb (no to) to say that you ask or tell someone to do something, usually because it's their job. It sounds formal or businesslike: I'll have my assistant call you.
examples: I'll have my assistant call you tomorrow.
The teacher had us read the text aloud.
We'll have the porter carry your bags.

uk.explanation: Have + person + base verb (без to) означає, що ви просите чи доручаєте комусь щось зробити, зазвичай тому, що це його робота. Звучить офіційно чи по-діловому: I'll have my assistant call you.
examples: Завтра мій помічник вам подзвонить.
Учитель попросив нас прочитати текст уголос.
Портьє віднесе ваші сумки.

745.explanation: Use the past continuous for a longer action that was going on in the background, and the past simple for the main event that happened in the middle of it. The pattern is was / were + -ing, often with when or while.
examples: I was having a shower when the phone rang.
It was raining when we left the cinema.
While she was cooking, the lights went out.

uk.explanation: Past continuous вживаємо для довшої дії, яка відбувалася на тлі, а past simple — для головної події, що сталася посеред неї. Схема — was / were + -ing, часто з when або while.

746.explanation: Use the past continuous for an action that was in progress at a particular time in the past. It had started and had not finished yet. The pattern is was / were + -ing.
examples: At eight o'clock we were having dinner.
What were you doing last night at ten?
It was snowing all morning.

uk.explanation: Past continuous вживаємо для дії, яка тривала в певний момент у минулому: вона вже почалася і ще не закінчилася. Схема — was / were + -ing.

750.explanation: The past continuous can explain why something happened: the situation that was going on was the reason. It often comes after because or as: because + subject + was / were + -ing.
examples: I didn't answer because I was driving.
She was tired because she was working late every night.
As we were walking past, we decided to go in.

uk.explanation: Past continuous може пояснювати, чому щось сталося: причиною була ситуація, що тоді тривала. Часто стоїть після because або as: because + subject + was / were + -ing.

751.explanation: Use the past continuous with always to talk about something that happened again and again over a period in the past. Always goes between was / were and the -ing verb.
examples: In winter it was always raining.
He was always talking about football.
My grandmother was always baking something.

uk.explanation: Past continuous з always вживаємо, щоб сказати, що щось повторювалося знову і знову протягом певного часу в минулому. Always стоїть між was / were і дієсловом з -ing.

753.explanation: I was wondering if… and I was thinking… make a request or suggestion softer and more polite. You mean now, but the past form sounds less direct.
examples: I was wondering if you could help me.
I was thinking we could meet on Friday.
I was wondering if I could borrow your car.

uk.explanation: I was wondering if… та I was thinking… роблять прохання або пропозицію м'якшими й ввічливішими. Ідеться про теперішнє, але минула форма звучить менш прямо.

754.explanation: Use the past continuous with always or constantly to complain about something that happened again and again and was annoying or out of control. The pattern is was / were + always / constantly + -ing.
examples: He was constantly interrupting me.
She was always losing her keys.
They were always arguing about money.

uk.explanation: Past continuous з always або constantly вживаємо, щоб поскаржитися на те, що повторювалося знову і знову, дратувало або не піддавалося контролю. Схема — was / were + always / constantly + -ing.

756.explanation: Use the past perfect continuous for a background action that started earlier and was still going on when the main event happened. The pattern is had been + -ing; the main event is in the past simple.
examples: We had been walking for hours when it started to rain.
She had been sleeping when the alarm went off.
I had been waiting a long time when he finally called.

uk.explanation: Past perfect continuous вживаємо для фонової дії, яка почалася раніше й досі тривала, коли сталася головна подія. Схема — had been + -ing; головна подія — у past simple.

757.explanation: Use the past perfect continuous for an action that started before a past moment and continued up to it. We often say how long with for or since: had been + -ing + for / since.
examples: He had been working there for ten years.
They had been living in Lviv since 2015.
I had been learning English for two years before the trip.

uk.explanation: Past perfect continuous вживаємо для дії, яка почалася до певного моменту в минулому і тривала аж до нього. Часто кажемо, як довго, з for або since: had been + -ing + for / since.

758.explanation: You can use the past perfect continuous in a relative clause to add background about someone or something. The pattern is who / which / that + had been + -ing.
examples: The man who had been sitting next to me got off.
The dog, which had been barking all night, was finally quiet.
I met a woman who had been travelling for a year.

uk.explanation: Past perfect continuous можна вжити в підрядному означальному реченні, щоб додати фонову інформацію про когось чи щось. Схема — who / which / that + had been + -ing.

759.explanation: You can use the past perfect continuous after a time word like after, when, since or until to give background. The pattern is after / when + subject + had been + -ing.
examples: After we had been driving for an hour, we stopped for coffee.
When she had been studying for months, she finally passed.
Since he had been feeling ill, he stayed at home.

uk.explanation: Past perfect continuous можна вжити після слова часу, як-от after, when, since чи until, щоб дати фонову інформацію. Схема — after / when + subject + had been + -ing.

762.explanation: Use the past perfect continuous for an activity that had finished, but its results were still clear at a later past moment. The pattern is had been + -ing.
examples: Her eyes were red because she had been crying.
The ground was wet. It had been raining.
He was tired because he had been running.

uk.explanation: Past perfect continuous вживаємо для дії, яка вже закінчилася, але її наслідки ще було видно в пізніший момент у минулому. Схема — had been + -ing.

764.explanation: Use the past perfect after if to imagine a different past, often when you feel sorry about it. The pattern is if + had + past participle, would have + past participle.
examples: If I had known, I would have called you.
If we had left earlier, we wouldn't have missed the bus.
If she had asked me, I would have helped.

uk.explanation: Past perfect після if вживаємо, щоб уявити інше минуле, часто коли шкодуємо про нього. Схема — if + had + past participle, would have + past participle.

768.explanation: Use the past perfect to show that one thing happened before another time in the past. The pattern is had + past participle.
examples: When we arrived, the film had already started.
I had never seen snow before that winter.
She had finished her work by six.

uk.explanation: Past perfect вживаємо, щоб показати, що одна подія сталася раніше за інший момент у минулому. Схема — had + past participle.

769.explanation: Use the past perfect after because to explain a past situation with something that happened earlier. The pattern is because + subject + had + past participle.
examples: I was hungry because I hadn't eaten all day.
He failed because he hadn't studied.
We were late because we had missed the train.

uk.explanation: Past perfect після because вживаємо, щоб пояснити ситуацію в минулому тим, що сталося ще раніше. Схема — because + subject + had + past participle.

770.explanation: Use the past perfect after wish or if only to say you are sorry about something in the past. The pattern is wish / if only + subject + had (not) + past participle.
examples: I wish I had studied harder.
If only we had booked a table!
She wishes she hadn't said that.

uk.explanation: Past perfect після wish або if only вживаємо, щоб сказати, що шкодуємо про щось у минулому. Схема — wish / if only + subject + had (not) + past participle.

771.explanation: In formal English, you can start with never or never before and then put had before the subject. This shows that an event was unique. The pattern is never (before) + had + subject + past participle.
examples: Never before had I seen such a crowd.
Never had she felt so alone.
Never before had the city looked so beautiful.

uk.explanation: В офіційній англійській можна почати з never або never before, а потім поставити had перед підметом. Так показуємо, що подія була єдиною у своєму роді. Схема — never (before) + had + subject + past participle.

772.explanation: No sooner … than shows that one thing happened right after another. It is formal, and had goes before the subject: no sooner + had + subject + past participle + than + past simple.
examples: No sooner had I sat down than the phone rang.
No sooner had we arrived than it started to rain.
No sooner had she left than he called.

uk.explanation: No sooner … than показує, що одна подія сталася одразу після іншої. Це офіційний стиль, і had стоїть перед підметом: no sooner + had + subject + past participle + than + past simple.

776.explanation: You can use the past perfect in a relative clause to add background about something that happened earlier. The pattern is who / which / that + had + past participle.
examples: I returned the book that I had borrowed.
We visited the town where my father had grown up.
The man who had helped us was gone.

uk.explanation: Past perfect можна вжити в підрядному означальному реченні, щоб додати фонову інформацію про те, що сталося раніше. Схема — who / which / that + had + past participle.

777.explanation: Use the past perfect to show that a situation was different before it changed. The earlier situation uses had + past participle, and the change often comes with but or then.
examples: I had always lived in the city, but then we moved.
She had never liked fish, but now she loves it.
We had planned a picnic, but it rained.

uk.explanation: Past perfect вживаємо, щоб показати, що до зміни ситуація була іншою. Попередня ситуація — had + past participle, а зміна часто вводиться через but або then.

778.explanation: When you report a question with a past verb like asked or wanted to know, a past simple or present perfect question often becomes past perfect. The pattern is asked + if / wh-word + subject + had + past participle.
examples: She asked me if I had seen the film.
He wanted to know where I had been.
They asked if we had finished.

uk.explanation: Коли переказуємо запитання з дієсловом у минулому, як-от asked чи wanted to know, запитання в past simple або present perfect часто переходить у past perfect. Схема — asked + if / wh-word + subject + had + past participle.

779.explanation: When you report what someone said with a past verb like said or told, a past simple or present perfect often becomes past perfect. The pattern is said (that) + subject + had + past participle.
examples: She said she had lost her phone.
He told me he had already eaten.
They said they had never been to Kyiv.

uk.explanation: Коли переказуємо чиїсь слова з дієсловом у минулому, як-от said чи told, past simple або present perfect часто переходить у past perfect. Схема — said (that) + subject + had + past participle.

780.explanation: In formal English, you can drop if and put had first to imagine a different past, often with regret. The pattern is had + subject + past participle, would have + past participle.
examples: Had I known, I would have come earlier.
Had we left on time, we would have caught the train.
Had she asked, I would have helped her.

uk.explanation: В офіційній англійській можна прибрати if і поставити had на початок, щоб уявити інше минуле, часто з жалем. Схема — had + subject + past participle, would have + past participle.

781.explanation: Use if only with the negative past perfect to say you strongly regret something that happened. The pattern is if only + subject + hadn't + past participle.
examples: If only I hadn't said that!
If only we hadn't sold the house.
If only she hadn't missed the train.

uk.explanation: If only із заперечною формою past perfect вживаємо, щоб сказати, що дуже шкодуємо про те, що сталося. Схема — if only + subject + hadn't + past participle.

785.explanation: Use the past simple for things that happened or were true at a finished time in the past. Regular verbs add -ed; many common verbs are irregular.
examples: I watched TV last night.
We went to the park yesterday.
She was happy.

uk.explanation: Past simple вживаємо для того, що сталося або було правдою в минулому, у час, який уже закінчився. Правильні дієслова додають -ed; багато поширених дієслів — неправильні.

793.explanation: Use the past simple for habits or states that were true for a period in the past but are not true now. The verb is in the past simple, often with every day or when I was a child.
examples: We lived by the sea when I was small.
He walked to school every day.
I played football every weekend.

uk.explanation: Past simple вживаємо для звичок або станів, які були правдою певний час у минулому, але тепер уже ні. Дієслово — у past simple, часто з every day або when I was a child.

794.explanation: Use the past simple after if to imagine a situation now or in the future that is not real or not likely. The pattern is if + past simple, would + verb.
examples: If I had more money, I would buy a car.
If you asked him, he would help.
If we lived closer, we would visit more often.

uk.explanation: Past simple після if вживаємо, щоб уявити ситуацію тепер або в майбутньому, яка не є реальною чи малоймовірна. Схема — if + past simple, would + verb.

795.explanation: In a story, use a series of past simple verbs to tell events in the order they happened. Words like first, then and after that help.
examples: He opened the door, looked in and smiled.
First we had lunch, then we went to the beach.
She got up, dressed and left.

uk.explanation: В оповіді ряд дієслів у past simple передає події в тому порядку, в якому вони сталися. Допомагають слова first, then і after that.

796.explanation: Use wish with the past simple to say you want something now to be different. The pattern is wish (that) + subject + past simple.
examples: I wish I had a bigger flat.
I wish I knew the answer.
She wishes she lived near the sea.

uk.explanation: Wish з past simple вживаємо, щоб сказати, що хочемо, аби щось у теперішньому було інакше. Схема — wish (that) + subject + past simple.

801.explanation: In polite letters and emails, use the past simple after if to make a request softer. The pattern is I would be grateful if you + past simple.
examples: I would be grateful if you sent me the details.
It would be great if you called me back.
I would appreciate it if you replied soon.

uk.explanation: У ввічливих листах і емейлах past simple після if робить прохання м'якшим. Схема — I would be grateful if you + past simple.

802.explanation: I wondered if… and I wanted to… are polite ways to ask for something or to thank someone. You mean now, but the past form sounds less direct.
examples: I wondered if you could help me.
I wanted to thank you for the flowers.
I wondered if you were free on Friday.

uk.explanation: I wondered if… та I wanted to… — ввічливі способи про щось попросити або подякувати. Ідеться про теперішнє, але минула форма звучить менш прямо.

805.explanation: In more complex stories, the past simple can order events with time words like as soon as, once, the moment or by the time. The verbs in both parts are usually in the past simple.
examples: As soon as she saw him, she started to cry.
The moment I opened the door, the dog ran out.
Once we paid, we left the restaurant.

uk.explanation: У складніших оповідях past simple може впорядковувати події зі словами часу, як-от as soon as, once, the moment чи by the time. Дієслова в обох частинах зазвичай у past simple.

806.explanation: Put did before the main verb to make a past statement stronger, often when someone doubts it. The pattern is did + verb, with stress on did.
examples: I did call you, but you didn't answer.
She did finish the report in the end.
We did enjoy the party.

uk.explanation: Did перед основним дієсловом робить твердження про минуле сильнішим, часто коли хтось у ньому сумнівається. Схема — did + verb, наголос на did.

807.explanation: I thought… makes a suggestion or opinion sound softer and less direct. You mean now, but the past form sounds more polite.
examples: I thought we could go for a walk.
I thought you might like this book.
I thought it would be nice to invite them.

uk.explanation: I thought… робить пропозицію чи думку м'якшою й менш прямою. Ідеться про теперішнє, але минула форма звучить ввічливіше.

810.explanation: Use the present perfect continuous for an activity that you have done again and again from some time in the past until now. The pattern is have / has been + -ing.
examples: I've been going to the gym a lot lately.
She has been calling me every day.
We've been meeting on Fridays since May.

uk.explanation: Present perfect continuous вживаємо для дії, яку робимо знову і знову від певного моменту в минулому дотепер. Схема — have / has been + -ing.

811.explanation: Use the present perfect continuous for one activity that started in the past and is still going on now. We often say how long with for or since: have / has been + -ing.
examples: I've been waiting for an hour.
She has been living here since 2020.
How long have you been learning English?

uk.explanation: Present perfect continuous вживаємо для однієї дії, яка почалася в минулому й триває досі. Часто кажемо, як довго, з for або since: have / has been + -ing.

814.explanation: Use the present perfect continuous for an activity that has just finished when you can still see its results. The pattern is have / has been + -ing.
examples: I'm tired because I've been running.
Your eyes are red. Have you been crying?
It's been raining — the street is wet.

uk.explanation: Present perfect continuous вживаємо для дії, яка щойно закінчилася, коли ще видно її наслідки. Схема — have / has been + -ing.

815.explanation: In formal English, you can start with not only and put have / has before the subject to make a point stand out. The pattern is not only + have / has + subject + been + -ing, but (also)….
examples: Not only have prices been rising, but wages have also fallen.
Not only has she been working, but she's been studying too.
Not only have they been ignoring us, but they have also lied.

uk.explanation: В офіційній англійській можна почати з not only і поставити have / has перед підметом, щоб виділити думку. Схема — not only + have / has + subject + been + -ing, but (also)….

816.explanation: Use the negative present perfect with for to say something has not happened during a period up to now. The pattern is haven't / hasn't + past participle + for + time.
examples: I haven't seen her for years.
We haven't eaten out for a month.
He hasn't called me for weeks.

uk.explanation: Заперечну форму present perfect з for вживаємо, щоб сказати, що щось не відбувалося протягом певного часу дотепер. Схема — haven't / hasn't + past participle + for + time.

817.explanation: Use the negative present perfect with yet for something you expect to happen, but it hasn't happened so far. Yet goes at the end: haven't / hasn't + past participle + yet.
examples: I haven't finished my homework yet.
The bus hasn't come yet.
She hasn't replied yet.

uk.explanation: Заперечну форму present perfect з yet вживаємо для того, що має статися, але поки що не сталося. Yet стоїть у кінці: haven't / hasn't + past participle + yet.

822.explanation: Use the present perfect to talk about experiences in your life up to now, when the exact time is not important. We often use ever and never: have / has + past participle.
examples: Have you ever been to London?
I've never eaten sushi.
She has visited Paris twice.

uk.explanation: Present perfect вживаємо, щоб розповісти про досвід у житті дотепер, коли точний час не важливий. Часто вживаємо ever і never: have / has + past participle.

823.explanation: Use the present perfect with since to say when a situation started, if it is still true now. The pattern is have / has + past participle + since + a point in time.
examples: I've lived here since 2020.
We have known each other since school.
She has worked here since March.

uk.explanation: Present perfect із since вживаємо, щоб сказати, коли почалася ситуація, яка триває досі. Схема — have / has + past participle + since + момент у часі.

824.explanation: Use the present perfect with already to show that something is done, often sooner than expected. Already usually goes between have / has and the past participle.
examples: I've already done the shopping.
She has already left.
Have you already eaten?

uk.explanation: Present perfect з already вживаємо, щоб показати, що щось уже зроблено, часто раніше, ніж очікували. Already зазвичай стоїть між have / has і past participle.

829.explanation: Use the present perfect for something that happened a short time ago and matters now. Just often goes between have / has and the past participle.
examples: I've just finished my lunch.
She has just arrived.
Oh no, I've lost my keys!

uk.explanation: Present perfect вживаємо для того, що сталося недавно і важливе зараз. Just часто стоїть між have / has і past participle.

830.explanation: Use the present perfect for a state or period that started in the past and has no clear end — it is still true now. The pattern is have / has + past participle.
examples: I've always loved music.
People have lived here for centuries.
She has been my best friend for years.

uk.explanation: Present perfect вживаємо для стану чи періоду, який почався в минулому і не має чіткого кінця — він досі правдивий. Схема — have / has + past participle.

831.explanation: Use the present perfect after a superlative to say that something is the best or worst in your experience so far. The pattern is the + superlative + noun + I have ever + past participle.
examples: It's the best film I've ever seen.
This is the worst meal I've ever eaten.
She's the kindest person I've ever met.

uk.explanation: Present perfect після найвищого ступеня прикметника вживаємо, щоб сказати, що щось найкраще чи найгірше в нашому досвіді дотепер. Схема — the + superlative + noun + I have ever + past participle.

832.explanation: Use still with the negative present perfect when something was expected to happen but still hasn't. Still goes before haven't / hasn't: still + haven't / hasn't + past participle.
examples: I still haven't got my money back.
He still hasn't called me.
We still haven't found a flat.

uk.explanation: Still із заперечною формою present perfect вживаємо, коли щось мало статися, але досі не сталося. Still стоїть перед haven't / hasn't: still + haven't / hasn't + past participle.

835.explanation: News reports often start with the present perfect to say that something new has happened. The details that follow are usually in the past simple.
examples: A new bridge has opened in the city centre.
Scientists have found water on the planet.
The president has arrived in Kyiv.

uk.explanation: Новини часто починаються з present perfect, щоб повідомити, що сталося щось нове. Подробиці далі зазвичай подаються в past simple.

848.explanation: In formal writing, put the preposition before which, whom or whose instead of at the end of the clause: the person to whom I spoke. This avoids leaving the preposition at the end, but sounds more formal than everyday speech.
examples: This is the club of which you are the secretary.
She is someone to whom I owe a lot.
It is a position in which I am very interested.

uk.explanation: В офіційному письмі прийменник ставлять перед which, whom чи whose, а не в кінці речення: the person to whom I spoke. Так прийменник не лишається в кінці, але це звучить офіційніше за повсякденну мову.
examples: Це клуб, секретарем якого ви є.
Це людина, якій я багато чим завдячую.
Це посада, яка мене дуже цікавить.

849.explanation: Some one-word prepositions, like upon, amongst, amid, beneath and towards, are rare in everyday speech but common in formal, literary or business writing. They often replace a more common word: upon = on.
examples: Please act upon the advice you were given.
A survey was carried out amongst the students.
The house stood beneath a tall old tree.

uk.explanation: Деякі однослівні прийменники, як-от upon, amongst, amid, beneath і towards, рідко звучать у повсякденному мовленні, але часто трапляються в офіційному, літературному чи діловому письмі. Часто вони замінюють звичніше слово: upon = on.
examples: Будь ласка, дійте відповідно до наданої вам поради.
Серед студентів провели опитування.
Будинок стояв під високим старим деревом.

850.explanation: Longer complex prepositions, like on account of, ahead of, with regard to and in accordance with, are typical of formal, literary or business writing. They often replace a shorter, more common word: on account of = because of.
examples: The meeting was postponed on account of the strike.
The company launched the product ahead of its rivals.
We are writing with regard to your recent order.

uk.explanation: Довші складені прийменники, як-от on account of, ahead of, with regard to та in accordance with, типові для офіційного, літературного чи ділового письма. Часто вони замінюють коротше й звичніше слово: on account of = because of.
examples: Зустріч перенесли через страйк.
Компанія випустила продукт раніше за конкурентів.
Пишемо вам щодо вашого нещодавнього замовлення.

852.explanation: Use the present continuous for something that is happening now, at the moment of speaking. The pattern is am / is / are + -ing.
examples: I'm reading a book.
She is cooking dinner.
What are you doing?

uk.explanation: Present continuous вживаємо для того, що відбувається зараз, у момент мовлення. Схема — am / is / are + -ing.

855.explanation: You can use the present continuous with always to talk about something that happens a lot, often when it surprises or annoys you. Always goes between am / is / are and the -ing verb.
examples: He's always losing his phone.
You're always complaining!
My sister is always borrowing my clothes.

uk.explanation: Present continuous з always вживаємо, щоб сказати, що щось стається дуже часто, зазвичай коли це дивує чи дратує. Always стоїть між am / is / are і дієсловом з -ing.

856.explanation: Use the present continuous for actions and situations that are happening now or around now. The pattern is am / is / are + -ing, and it works with many kinds of verbs.
examples: The children are playing in the garden.
We're looking for a new flat.
Is it still raining outside?

uk.explanation: Present continuous вживаємо для дій і ситуацій, що відбуваються зараз або приблизно в цей час. Схема — am / is / are + -ing, і вона працює з багатьма дієсловами.

857.explanation: Use the present continuous for a situation that is true now but only for a short time. The pattern is am / is / are + -ing, often with at the moment or this week.
examples: I'm staying with my aunt this week.
She's working from home at the moment.
We're living in a small flat for now.

uk.explanation: Present continuous вживаємо для ситуації, яка правдива зараз, але лише на короткий час. Схема — am / is / are + -ing, часто з at the moment або this week.

858.explanation: Use the present continuous for something you do regularly, but only for a limited time. The pattern is am / is / are + -ing, often with these days or this month.
examples: I'm going to the gym every day this month.
He's getting up early these days.
We're eating less meat at the moment.

uk.explanation: Present continuous вживаємо для того, що робимо регулярно, але лише обмежений час. Схема — am / is / are + -ing, часто з these days або this month.

859.explanation: Use the present continuous for actions and situations in progress now, including longer changes. The pattern is am / is / are + -ing, and it works with a wide range of verbs.
examples: The city is growing very fast.
More people are working from home.
Prices are going up again.

uk.explanation: Present continuous вживаємо для дій і ситуацій, що тривають зараз, зокрема для довших змін. Схема — am / is / are + -ing, і вона працює з широким колом дієслів.

860.explanation: Use the present continuous for temporary situations, not permanent ones. The pattern is am / is / are + -ing, and it works with a wide range of verbs.
examples: My brother is studying in Poland this year.
I'm using my old laptop while mine is repaired.
She's teaching at a school in Odesa for a year.

uk.explanation: Present continuous вживаємо для тимчасових ситуацій, а не постійних. Схема — am / is / are + -ing, і вона працює з широким колом дієслів.

861.explanation: The present continuous goes with adverbs like constantly, continually and forever to show that something happens a lot, often in an annoying way. The adverb goes between am / is / are and the -ing verb.
examples: He's constantly checking his phone.
They're forever arguing about money.
She's continually changing her mind.

uk.explanation: Present continuous поєднується з прислівниками на кшталт constantly, continually та forever, щоб показати, що щось стається дуже часто, зазвичай дратівливо. Прислівник стоїть між am / is / are і дієсловом з -ing.

862.explanation: You can ask a question in the present continuous that does not need an answer, to show surprise or criticism. The pattern is question word + am / is / are + subject + -ing.
examples: What are you doing? That's my coffee!
Who are you calling lazy?
Are you joking?

uk.explanation: Можна поставити запитання в present continuous, яке не потребує відповіді, щоб висловити подив чи критику. Схема — question word + am / is / are + subject + -ing.

863.explanation: The present continuous goes with many adverbs of frequency, including perpetually and incessantly, to show that something happens a lot and is annoying or out of control. The adverb goes between am / is / are and the -ing verb.
examples: He is perpetually complaining about his job.
The neighbours are incessantly arguing.
She's eternally worrying about something.

uk.explanation: Present continuous поєднується з багатьма прислівниками частоти, зокрема perpetually та incessantly, щоб показати, що щось стається дуже часто, дратує чи не піддається контролю. Прислівник стоїть між am / is / are і дієсловом з -ing.

864.explanation: Verbs like hope, want or wonder are not usually continuous, but the present continuous makes a request or statement softer and less direct. The pattern is I'm hoping / wondering / wanting + rest.
examples: I'm hoping you can help me.
We're wanting to leave early, if that's OK.
I'm wondering whether to accept the offer.

uk.explanation: Дієслова на кшталт hope, want чи wonder зазвичай не вживаються в тривалій формі, але present continuous робить прохання чи твердження м'якшим і менш прямим. Схема — I'm hoping / wondering / wanting + решта речення.

868.explanation: Use the present simple for habits, things that happen again and again, and general facts. Add -s or -es after he, she, it: she works.
examples: I get up at seven every day.
She plays tennis on Sundays.
Water boils at 100 degrees.

uk.explanation: Present simple вживаємо для звичок, того, що повторюється, і загальних фактів. Після he, she, it додаємо -s або -es: she works.

869.explanation: Use the present simple after if for a situation that can really happen, and say what will follow. The pattern is if + present simple, will / can / imperative + verb.
examples: If it rains, we'll stay at home.
If you're hungry, eat something.
If you want, I can help you.

uk.explanation: Present simple після if вживаємо для ситуації, яка справді може статися, і кажемо, що з цього вийде. Схема — if + present simple, will / can / imperative + verb.

875.explanation: Use the present simple to explain steps or give directions. Each step is a present simple verb, often with you or with first and then.
examples: You turn left at the bank.
First you open the app, then you click Start.
You take the second street on the right.

uk.explanation: Present simple вживаємо, щоб пояснити кроки або показати дорогу. Кожен крок — дієслово в present simple, часто з you або з first і then.

876.explanation: Verbs about thinking, like think, hope and know, are usually in the present simple, not the continuous. The pattern is subject + think / hope / know + rest.
examples: I think it's a good idea.
I hope you feel better soon.
Do you know her name?

uk.explanation: Дієслова мислення, як-от think, hope і know, зазвичай уживаються в present simple, а не в тривалій формі. Схема — subject + think / hope / know + решта речення.

877.explanation: Use Why don't you / we…? or if you want / if you like with the present simple to suggest something in a friendly way. The pattern is Why don't you / we + verb?
examples: Why don't we go to the cinema?
Why don't you ask your teacher?
We can meet later, if you like.

uk.explanation: Why don't you / we…? або if you want / if you like з present simple вживаємо, щоб дружньо щось запропонувати. Схема — Why don't you / we + verb?

878.explanation: Add don't you think? or don't you agree? to your opinion to ask someone to agree with you. It usually comes at the end, after a comma.
examples: It's a great film, don't you think?
She's very talented, don't you agree?
Don't you think it's too expensive?

uk.explanation: Don't you think? або don't you agree? після своєї думки вживаємо, щоб попросити співрозмовника погодитися. Зазвичай стоїть у кінці, після коми.

880.explanation: Verbs about the mind, like remember, understand and believe, are usually in the present simple. The pattern is subject + remember / understand / believe + rest.
examples: I remember our first meeting.
Do you understand the question?
I don't believe his story.

uk.explanation: Дієслова про розумові процеси, як-от remember, understand і believe, зазвичай уживаються в present simple. Схема — subject + remember / understand / believe + решта речення.

881.explanation: Use the present simple with verbs like say and show to tell what a text, sign or picture says. The pattern is the sign / letter / map + says / shows + that.
examples: The sign says 'No parking'.
The map shows where the station is.
His letter says that he is fine.

uk.explanation: Present simple з дієсловами на кшталт say і show вживаємо, щоб передати, що каже текст, табличка чи малюнок. Схема — the sign / letter / map + says / shows + that.

882.explanation: Some verbs do an action when you say them, like suggest, apologise and recommend. Use them in the present simple with I: I suggest…, I apologise for…
examples: I suggest we take a taxi.
I apologise for being late.
I recommend the fish soup.

uk.explanation: Деякі дієслова виконують дію вже тим, що їх вимовляють, як-от suggest, apologise і recommend. Уживаємо їх у present simple з I: I suggest…, I apologise for…

884.explanation: Many verbs, like agree, accept and advise, do an action when you say them. Use them in the present simple with I or we: I agree…, I advise you to….
examples: I agree with you completely.
We accept your offer.
I advise you to see a doctor.

uk.explanation: Багато дієслів, як-от agree, accept і advise, виконують дію вже тим, що їх вимовляють. Уживаємо їх у present simple з I або we: I agree…, I advise you to….

885.explanation: You can use the present simple to retell a story, film or piece of history, so it feels more immediate. All the main events are in the present simple.
examples: In the film, a boy finds a dog and takes it home.
In 1492, Columbus sails west and reaches America.
The hero wakes up and realises he is alone.

uk.explanation: Present simple можна вжити, щоб переказати історію, фільм чи подію з минулого, — так розповідь звучить живіше. Усі основні події подаються в present simple.

886.explanation: A negative question can persuade someone to agree with you, because it suggests the answer is yes. The pattern is Don't / Doesn't + subject + verb…?
examples: Don't you want to be healthy?
Doesn't everyone deserve a second chance?
Don't we all need a holiday?

uk.explanation: Заперечне запитання може переконати співрозмовника погодитися, бо натякає, що відповідь — так. Схема — Don't / Doesn't + subject + verb…?

887.explanation: A negative question can check whether someone shares your opinion. The pattern is Don't / Doesn't + subject + think / agree / find…?
examples: Don't you find this music a bit loud?
Doesn't she think it's too late?
Don't you agree that he was wrong?

uk.explanation: Заперечне запитання може перевірити, чи поділяє співрозмовник нашу думку. Схема — Don't / Doesn't + subject + think / agree / find…?

888.explanation: In academic writing, use the present simple with reporting verbs like demonstrate, illustrate and argue to say what a study or writer shows. The pattern is the study / author + demonstrates / argues + that.
examples: The study demonstrates that sleep improves memory.
This example illustrates the problem clearly.
The author argues that cities need more parks.

uk.explanation: В академічному письмі present simple з дієсловами переказу, як-от demonstrate, illustrate і argue, вживаємо, щоб сказати, що показує дослідження чи автор. Схема — the study / author + demonstrates / argues + that.

903.explanation: Put this or that before a noun + of + possessive pronoun to show a feeling about someone's thing: that car of yours. It often sounds annoyed, ironic or funny, sometimes warm. It is typical of stories and informal speech.
examples: You can park that precious jeep of yours over there.
I didn't like that new girlfriend of his.
I want this dream of mine to come true.

uk.explanation: This або that перед іменником + of + присвійний займенник показує ставлення до чиєїсь речі: that car of yours. Часто це звучить роздратовано, іронічно чи смішно, інколи тепло. Це типово для оповідей і розмовного мовлення.

909.explanation: Use by + myself, yourself, himself or herself to mean alone, or without any help. The situation tells you which meaning.
examples: He tried to open it by himself.
I will study by myself at home.
She lives by herself in a small flat.

uk.explanation: By + myself, yourself, himself або herself означає «сам, наодинці» або «без жодної допомоги». Яке значення — видно з ситуації.

912.explanation: Use myself, yourself, himself or herself to stress who did something: this person and nobody else. It usually goes at the end of the clause or straight after the noun: I made it myself.
examples: The cake was delicious. Sandra made it herself.
You should decide what to do yourself.
The director himself showed us round the school.

uk.explanation: Myself, yourself, himself або herself підкреслюють, хто саме щось зробив: ця людина, а не хтось інший. Зазвичай стоїть у кінці частини речення або одразу після іменника: I made it myself.

913.explanation: Use by + ourselves, yourselves or themselves to mean alone as a group, or without any help: just us, you or them, nobody else.
examples: My friend and I are planning a holiday by ourselves.
I think you will find it by yourselves.
Suddenly, the windows opened by themselves.

uk.explanation: By + ourselves, yourselves або themselves означає «самі, групою без інших» або «без жодної допомоги»: лише ми, ви чи вони, більше ніхто.

917.explanation: Use the fixed phrase in itself to mean "on its own, without anything else". It makes the point stronger and usually comes after be + adjective or after the noun.
examples: The house in itself is beautiful.
A car can't be harmful in itself.
Spending time with family is important in itself.

uk.explanation: Сталий вираз in itself означає «сам по собі, без нічого іншого». Він підсилює думку й зазвичай стоїть після be + прикметник або після іменника.

918.explanation: Put itself straight after a noun to stress the thing itself, not the things around it: the building itself.
examples: The building itself looks splendid.
The story itself must be good.
The town itself is small, but the area is huge.

uk.explanation: Itself одразу після іменника підкреслює саму річ, а не те, що довкола неї: the building itself.

919.explanation: Use ourselves, yourselves or themselves to stress who did something: these people and nobody else. Put it at the end of the clause or straight after the noun.
examples: Sometimes we can cook something ourselves.
They were very busy themselves.
Cars themselves are never dangerous.

uk.explanation: Ourselves, yourselves або themselves підкреслюють, хто саме щось зробив: ці люди, а не хтось інший. Ставте в кінці частини речення або одразу після іменника.

920.explanation: In formal letters and emails, some writers use yourselves instead of you to talk politely to a company or organisation. Plain you is always correct too.
examples: I am replying to the advert published by yourselves.
Training will be provided by yourselves, I believe.
Like yourselves, I live in a busy town.

uk.explanation: В офіційних листах та імейлах дехто вживає yourselves замість you, щоб увічливо звернутися до компанії чи організації. Просте you теж завжди правильне.

921.explanation: Use As for myself at the start of a sentence to move to your own opinion or situation after talking about other people. It is formal; in speaking, As for me is more usual.
examples: As for myself, I like taking responsibility.
As for myself, I grew up with the internet.
As for myself, I prefer quiet holidays.

uk.explanation: As for myself на початку речення переводить увагу на вашу власну думку чи ситуацію після розповіді про інших людей. Це офіційний вираз; в усному мовленні частіше кажуть As for me.

936.explanation: In formal writing, use it as the subject of a passive verb when who did the action is unknown or unimportant. The focus stays on the fact: It is hoped that…, It was decided that…
examples: It is hoped that this report will help the club.
It was decided that the meeting would be cancelled.
It is believed that the painting is very old.

uk.explanation: В офіційному письмі it може бути підметом пасивного дієслова, коли невідомо або неважливо, хто виконав дію. Увага лишається на самому факті: It is hoped that…, It was decided that…

939.explanation: Use this on its own to point to one thing you are going to show or explain right now. The information often comes straight after it, sometimes after a colon: This is + information.
examples: This is my phone number: 0754 567 7851.
Hi, Tom! This is Anna.
This is the plan: we meet at six.

uk.explanation: This без іменника вказує на одну річ, яку ви зараз покажете або поясните. Інформація часто йде одразу після нього, інколи після двокрапки: This is + інформація.
